title: sync: never replace non-empty remote content with a zero-length file

text.body:

Fixes #801

This PR:
- refuses to upload a zero-length file over non-empty remote content unless the user explicitly emptied it (tracked via the editor's last-save event)
- keeps the previous remote version in history instead of overwriting it in place
- adds an integration test that simulates sleep/offline mid-write

Recovery for users who were already hit is being handled server-side, separately.

title: Path traversal in .widgetpack import writes files outside the project

text.body:
**Summary**
`widget import <file>.widgetpack` does not sanitise entry names. An archive entry named `../../.bashrc` (or `..\..\AppData\...` on Windows) is written relative to the project folder, so importing a pack someone sends you can overwrite arbitrary files in your home directory.

**Affected**: 3.1.5 and 3.2.0-rc.1 (tested), probably everything since packs were added in 2.8.

**PoC**
```
python3 make_pack.py --entry '../../.bashrc' --content 'echo pwned' -o evil.widgetpack
widget import evil.widgetpack --into ~/widget/projects/test
tail -1 ~/.bashrc   # -> echo pwned
```
Same result when the pack is opened by double click in the desktop app.

**Impact**: code execution on next shell start for anyone who imports a shared pack. Packs are shared on the community forum a lot.

**Suggested fix**: reject entries whose normalised path escapes the target dir, refuse absolute paths and symlinks.

I have not published this anywhere else. Happy to test a patch.

gold.rationale: Report of "path traversal": "../" entries in an imported .widgetpack "overwrite arbitrary files in your home directory"; also labelled "security".

title: Scanner reports a CVE in the bundled zip library (confirmed false positive)

text.body:
Our compliance scanner flagged the zip library bundled in widget 3.2.0 for a CVE in its "streaming extract" function.
